submitted.rationale: Highest measured EQE: 0.122% at Cr0.16Sb0.84. EQE rose steadily toward the Sb-rich end: 0.0087% at Sb 0.49, 0.101% at Sb 0.77 and 0.122% at Sb 0.84.

rejected.reason: Near CrSbO4 stoichiometry; measured EQE only 0.0087%, despite a predicted near-hull phase with a ~2 eV gap.
Not measured. EQE fell steeply going from Sb-rich toward the 1:1 composition, so Cr-rich films are unlikely to beat the Sb-rich ones.

consultations.verdict: Support: CrSbO4 (Cr:Sb 1:1) is near-hull (0.065 eV/atom) with HSE gap ~2.0 eV, absorbing at 3.2 eV illumination; CrSb2O6 predicted less stable. Index 13 (Sb 0.49) targets the CrSbO4 stoichiometry.

Uninformative-to-weak: Sb-rich Cr3Sb5O16 predicted gap 0.88 eV (strong absorber but likely recombination-prone), Cr-rich Cr5Sb3O16 ~2.0 eV. The 1:1 composition was weak (0.0087%), so I am probing the Sb-rich end, where Cr-doped Sb oxide may behave differently, to map the line.

Uninformative: the CrSb2O6 polymorph's predicted gap is 0.75 eV, which does not explain the measured trend. The empirical trend (EQE rose from 0.0087% at Sb 0.49 to 0.10% at Sb 0.77) guides the choice: I am moving further toward Sb-rich (0.84), stopping short of the extreme end.
